label: copy-phase echo of y early in the copy (original positions 1-3, step <= 9)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only when the input token is y, i.e. the model has just fed back its own output y. Every activation has in_tok == y. It needs y to be an early original token (original position 0-2, so recall_idx 1-3) and the step to be early in absolute terms (t <= 9), which means short sequences (L 3-7). Magnitude is by far largest when y was the first original token, fed back right after <DEL> (recall_idx 1): this is 78% of activation mass and includes all top examples near 1.0. It is weaker at recall_idx 2 and 3 and weaker for longer L. Weak residual activations show up at t = 9-10 in L = 8 sequences. It never fires on y in the original phase, on <DEL>, on any other token, or on y fed back at later copy positions (recall_idx >= 4).

issues: Core claims check out on the dev profile: all activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000), all of it has in_tok == y (lift 32x), recall_idx is only 1-3 (mass 0.784/0.181/0.034), and there is zero activation at recall_idx >= 4, on <DEL>, or in the original phase. 'Weaker for longer L' also holds.

The cutoff t <= 9 is wrong in a systematic way. Where the feature stops firing depends on both L and recall_idx, not on absolute step. Dev precision for (in_tok==y, recall_idx=r, L): r=1 is 1.0 for L=3-7, 0.77 at L=8 (t=9), 0.09 at L=9 (t=10, outside the predicate). r=2 is about 1.0 for L=4-5, 0.87 at L=6, but 0.22 at L=7 (t=9, inside the predicate) and 0.008 at L=8 (t=10). r=3 is 0.70 at L=4, 0.48 at L=5, 0.16 at L=6 (t=9, inside the predicate) and 0.026 at L=7. So most of the 7711 test false positives are y fed back at recall_idx 2-3 with t=8-9 in longer sequences (e.g. 'v y l o r u g <DEL> v *y*', 'l v y 0 p w <DEL> l v *y*').

The cutoff tracks L + 2*recall_idx <= 10 (r=1 up to L=8, r=2 up to L=6, r=3 up to L=4), so the feature fades sooner at later recall positions. It is not a fixed step limit. Using this cutoff raises test precision from 0.765 to 0.925, and F1 from 0.861 to 0.910. Mass recall is 0.981.

The few remaining errors with the new cutoff are graded edge cases (r=3 L=5 at about 48%, weak activations below 0.3). They are not a new pattern. Whether y appeared earlier in the sequence (n_seen) made no difference.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase feedback of y from an early original position (recall_idx 1-3), firing only in short sequences. The allowed L shrinks as recall_idx grows (L + 2*recall_idx <= 10). Strongest for y as the first original token right after <DEL>.
